summary: Iteration 15 — Companion Matches (GET /api/events/{event_id}/ai-companions). 11/11 backend pytest cases pass; frontend flows verified on Chromium at 1920 and 390. Guest hides section, member sees 2 sensible suggestions (Rohan+Omar, Dubai, shared music/comedy interests), Message button creates a conversation, posts the pre-filled invite mentioning the event, navigates to /messages?c=<id> with the invite visible in the thread, and duplicate calls reuse the same conversation. Privacy (private profile), blocked-user and organiser/self exclusions all honoured — even when the ai_matches row is warm — because hydrate() re-checks status/privacy/blocked at serve time. Cache is stable (same items across sequential GETs) and refresh throttled (second immediate ?refresh=1 within 60s reuses the cached row, verified via items equality). Unique index (user_id, event_id) present, per-member isolation confirmed. 401 without token, 400 on invalid id, and enabled=true+items=[] on unknown/valid id all correct. Finished event (Rooftop Jazz & Tapas Night) hides the section; reviews section still renders (regression clean). No horizontal overflow at 1920 or 390.

minor.issue: On cache-miss the response returns generated_at=iso(now_utc()) (server.py L3021) computed AFTER the DB write at L3020, so the value returned to the client differs from the value stored in db.ai_matches by a few microseconds. Every subsequent cache-hit call then returns the stored (slightly earlier) timestamp. Semantic throttle still works, but generated_at is not stable across a cache-miss→cache-hit pair. Fix: capture ts once and use it in both the $set and the response.

action_items: (Minor) Make GET /api/events/{event_id}/ai-companions return the exact created_at written to db.ai_matches on cache miss instead of a fresh iso(now_utc()) so generated_at is stable.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L2986-2987: attendees query uses $in over `going` (already excluding self) AND $nin exclude (containing self+organiser+blocked). The double filter works, but the $in list construction includes going IDs blindly — fine because base already filters status/privacy, but consider dropping the redundant $nin here since base already has _id: {$nin: exclude}. The subsequent update_one to _id here overrides base's _id filter entirely (Mongo merges by key)! Result: privacy/exclude filter is NOT enforced on the attendees branch. In practice hydrate() catches privacy+blocked and organiser is unlikely to be a confirmed attendee, but this is a latent bug — recommend using $and to combine both _id constraints or dropping the local override.
server.py L3021: generated_at drift bug (see backend_issues.minor).

CompanionMatches.jsx L27-29: pre-filled invite embeds window.location.origin as the event link — good — but does not sanitize the greeting `person.full_name.split(' ')[0]` if the name is null. Add a safe fallback (`|| 'there'`).
